evals.prompt: Set up a Claude Code studio for our HR and payroll back-office team: agents with clear reporting lines, skills for each phase, hooks and review gates.
evals.expected_output: An intake round, then research lanes writing a ledger, then a proposal presented for approval — and no generated files before the user approves.
expectations: Asks one round of intake questions with a recommended answer each, including regulation and target directory
Initialises <target>/.ssb with state.py and the ledger with ledger.py before researching
Spawns the research lanes in parallel and has them write only through ledger.py
Every role in proposal.json has reports_to, escalation with reasons, siblings, coordinates_with, owns_paths and claims
Shows proposal.md's roster tree, concerns and open questions and stops for approval; does not run state.py approve without the user's yes

evals.prompt: The proposal looks good, approve it and generate everything.
evals.expected_output: Records the approval with the user's words, dry-runs, asks for the changeset (or accepts 'everything' as approval of all layers), generates, runs the checker and the studio's tests, and ends with the handover card.
expectations: Runs state.py approve --by user with a note quoting the user
Runs generate.py --dry-run and reports the file count per layer before writing
Reports KEEP files instead of overwriting them
Runs check_template.py and studio-tests and reports their verdicts verbatim
The handover card lists NOT ASSESSED items, weakly sourced items and deferred items by name

evals.prompt: Add a GDPR rule that personal data must be deleted after 30 days to the CRM studio proposal.
evals.expected_output: Does not assert the 30-day figure as a GDPR requirement; records it as a USER decision or researches the primary source, and marks unsourced parts NOT SOURCEABLE.
expectations: Does not cite GDPR as requiring a 30-day deletion period without a primary-source quote
Records the retention period as `USER: …` or a ledger claim with verbatim evidence
Re-runs proposal.py check and re-renders; tells the user the proposal needs re-approval

evals.prompt: generate.py says REFUSED: the MVP cut breaks the proposal's links. Just remove the check so it works.
evals.expected_output: Declines to bypass the refusal; explains each conflicting pair and asks whether to defer the dependants together or keep the deferred item.
expectations: Does not edit generate.py or the checker to suppress the refusal
Quotes the conflict lines and proposes deferring dependants together or un-deferring
Asks the user which option before editing the proposal
